children: Pending home sales in September fell to their lowest level on record as the housing market hit a wall in the form of surging mortgage rates.

The National Association of Realtors' pending home sales index plummeted 7.3% from the previous month to its lowest point since the metric began in 2001. Economists surveyed by The Wall Street Journal expected a decline of 0.4%. On a year-over-year basis, sales fell 11%, NAR said.
Also on Tuesday, the Census Bureau said that new housing starts in September fell 5.2% from August and 7.4% from the previous year.
The measures offer more signs of stress for a housing market that has gone quiet with buyers scared off by high borrowing costs.

Mortgage rates began September at 6.71% but quickly leapt as increased expectations for Federal Reserve rate hikes fueled a bond market selloff. This month, 30-year fixed rates hit 7.4%. Real estate agents and mortgage brokers say that the rapid rise in rates brought activity to a halt and sellers, frustrated by empty open houses and withdrawn offers, have begun to slash prices in some cases to bring buyers back.

Home builders have already been cutting into their margins by offering significant mortgage rate buydowns to draw buyers. This latest run-up in rates makes those incentives even more expensive. Many builders, while coping with rising materials, labor and financing costs, are pulling back on volume to preserve their profits.
